what_I_got_wrong: I called Storm@Portland a '31-point divergence where the MARKET prices the worse team (Seattle) as a coin flip / slight favorite,' based on the owner's board snapshot (Circa Storm -115, pick'em elsewhere). Injury acquisition (MEDIUM confidence, SI/sportsgambler) shows the CONSENSUS market actually has PORTLAND as the home favorite ~-125/-130 (~56%), Seattle +106. The market and the rating AGREE on the favorite (Portland); they disagree only on MAGNITUDE.
corrected_reading: The real gap is model ~74-80% (log5/Massey) vs market ~56% for the SAME side (Portland). It is mostly MODEL OVERCONFIDENCE — log5 over-maps a 3-rung rating gap between two weak teams (POR 12-19 #12, SEA 6-27 #15) to 74-80% in a single high-variance WNBA game; -125/-130 is normal moneyline compression. A real but SECONDARY effect: Portland's season rating is stale-HIGH (built partly on games featuring Barker + Feagin, both now season-ending ACLs, and Samuelson, foot-OUT), which should pull the rating DOWN toward the market. No Seattle catalyst exists (10-game skid, 2-16 SU road, cross-country trip). Net: narrow Portland toward ~56%; do NOT lay Portland heavily; this is NOT hidden Seattle value.
lesson: The owner's single-board snapshot was at the soft/opening end (one book slightly on Seattle). A single book != the market. And an injury-blind rating's confident number is not an edge — it over-extrapolates small rating gaps in high-variance sports. Both are exactly what the injury/odds acquisition was for.
caveat: Odds figures (~56% / ~74-80%) are betting-preview snippets, not a clean feed or the model's own output; verify posted odds + the official 5pm-prior WNBA injury report.
